utterances.text: Well, absolutely not for the same reasons that I explained earlier. I received my orders from my "komandir," commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We said that the police personnel who were members of the PJP received additional training, so could we please have Exhibit P1215 on our screens. So could you please tell us who issued this document and what is the date on it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The basic document was issued by the Ministry of the Interior and it is entitled: "Activities of the police members in case of armed attacks." And it was issued by the head of the public security sector in the Ministry of the Interior, and the cover letter from the police administration and the MUP that we can see precedes this very document forwarded this document to the units that are listed here in the text, and this was done by the assistant minister of the interior, Lieutenant-General Obrad Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So was this sent to people so that they take some action and also for their information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, information, analysis, and then implementation in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there any difference in the training of various groups within the PJP, do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In light of the fact that the members of the PJP were engaged in various tasks that I mentioned above, and that included tasks related to public law and order, bringing into custody perpetrators of dangerous crimes, and also fighting terrorist and sabotage activities, members of the PJP did receive training for each of these tasks separately, in order to be as well-prepared as possible to perform them up to the highest possible standard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And was there any additional training in the PJP for those units that were colloquially termed "OPG" [Realtime transcript read in error "OUP"], do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know something about that. I know that in early December 1998, or rather, in January 1999 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, just for the transcript, transcript records "colloquially termed OUP," in fact it should read OPG, that's operational pursuit groups?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, operational pursuit groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So from 1997, in what PJP unit did you serve and what duties did you perform there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I was the deputy company commander that was made up of police personnel from the secretariat of the interior in Cacak and Kraljevo. My company belonged to the 35th Detachment, headquartered in Uzice, and it was under the command of Lieutenant-General Branko Prljevic. He was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was lieutenant-colonel, not lieutenant-general, is that right, because --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, he was a lieutenant-colonel, not a lieutenant-general.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What duties did you perform in the actual fact?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: As I've already indicated, I was the deputy company commander and I was answerable for a part of that company, those people who had come from the Kraljevo secretariat of the interior, which was where I served usually.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You explained to us the strength of the company.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So how many people were there in your company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: My company - and I think that the other companies, too - would number 100 to 110 police officers at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now have Exhibit 1D401 in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is this document, Mr. Paunovic, or rather, what is the regulation or the ordinance that was published here in the Official Gazette that we see here in front of us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: This regulation is entitled: "Rules on the police uniform and insignia." It was issued pursuant to Article 19 of the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And can we see from this document who actually passed this regulation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we can see it quite clearly, that was the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us what uniforms were worn by PJP units in certain periods of time, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Police personnel wore uniforms that were strictly regulated, their type was strictly regulated, and they were adapted to the weather and the actual tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And could you please tell us what the colour was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: It depended on the field conditions, but the dominating colours were camouflage blue and camouflage green patterns worn in the field. Camouflage blue was primarily used in built-up areas, and the camouflage green pattern in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. If you haven't concluded, please continue.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: All types of uniforms had visible, clearly visible, insignia indicating that the personnel belonged to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, the Republic of Serbia flag, and other emblems that made it very easy to distinguish police personnel from other services.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Apart from the basic parts of uniform, did PJP members have any additional parts of uniform that were regulated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I think that this regulation and other regulations clearly defined the additional uniform parts and equipment to be used by PJP members. I would like to single out in particular protective vests, combat vests, protective helmets, helmets with protective eye plates, and other equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In 1998 was there a practice that was introduced for PJP members to use ribbons of various colours as a marking and why was this done?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning the terrorist activities that were launched in Kosovo and Metohija involved members of the terrorist units who used as their tactics dressing up as army and police personnel. And dressed in army and police uniforms, they would commit various crimes and atrocities in an effort to create an impression that those were committed by Ministry of the Interior personnel. On the other hand, it was very dangerous for the Ministry of the Interior personnel too. If you allow me, I can give you an example, a striking example, in which a police officer, a policeman, by the name of Perovic, and he was in fact an officer in the police in the Pec secretariat of the interior, he lost his life in an action in which the terrorists, members of the terrorist organizations, used police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have Exhibit 6D667 in e-court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm not clear whether these ribbons were used. I mean, I'm not finding that out for the answer, and why was this done? I mean, that's ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I explain?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. The question you were answering was whether there was a practice of using ribbons of various colours, but you didn't actually tell us whether there was. All you did was tell us about a terrorist atrocity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand your question and I will answer if you allow me, Your Honour. I was talking about the reason, the motive, behind this fact that members of the regular police, or rather, their leadership decided to use additional items, i.e., ribbons, to make a clear distinction between the regular police units and the terrorist groups that wore police uniforms as a rule when they perpetrated their crimes. And now motivated by this unfortunate incident in Pec and probably other crimes that had been committed, the leadership of the PJP decided that the police personnel should distinguish themselves from others and identify themselves in other ways by using those ribbons, and they would wear them on their right or left shoulder in accordance with the plan that was adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, thank you for your explanation. We have in front of us the document number 6D667, and could you please tell us what is this document and what is the date on this document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: This is the plan for marking the MUP and VJ units in the periods between the 25th and the 31st of July, 1998, where for each date it is designated in which manner the MUP and VJ members are to wear those ribbons, the colour is also designated, in order to be able to distinguish themselves from the other unlawful units and to identify themselves. So, for instance, we see in item 2, that's the 26th of July, 1998, it was indicated that -- it was designated that on that day a red ribbon should be tied to the left shoulder-strap and a white ribbon to the right shoulder-strap. The very next day and in the days that followed, the model changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have in e-court Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And could you please keep this document in front of you and we will have P1596 on our screens, please. We see it here now, we see the photograph. On the basis of the table that you have in front of you, can you tell us when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I notice that the members of the police who are on this photograph wore on the day when the photograph was taken a white ribbon on the right shoulder, or rather, a red ribbon on the left shoulder, on the basis of which I conclude that the photograph was probably taken on the 26th of July, 1998, when according to the plan of marking the MUP and VJ units it was stipulated that the members of the police should wear red ribbons on the left shoulder and white ribbons on the right shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the colour of uniform? In this photograph it is camouflage blue. Does that tell us something about the year when this was taken? Let's distinguish between 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm the year of 1998, when the uniforms also correspond to the said time-period, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the colour of the uniform of the man lying on the front of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you explain that through the uniform and additional gear, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Most of the members of the police in this photograph -- or may I say all of those who are standing and who are crouching in the second row and also one policeman who is lying on the ground, they're all wearing camouflage blue uniforms with additional gear, namely, a protective vest or a bullet-proof vest. I take the liberty of saying that there were three members of the police, there is a difference, one of the policemen is different. He is wearing a green camouflage combat vest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you saying that these are not all police officers or policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I am saying that these are policemen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's just there's a reference in the English translation at one point to saying that there are three members of the police, but it's maybe -- it's maybe corrected by you saying one is different. Is this your own company that we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should we start from the end then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, is this your company? No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's not my company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: From considering the document which we were looking at, do you know which VJ units were the subject of the plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I cannot give you a relevant answer to this question. I assume that it's all the units of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We've had senior officers of the army say that this never happened with soldiers. Are you actually aware of seeing soldiers in the field or in urban areas with ribbons on their shoulders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I saw members of the army who wore ribbons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, just in order to clarify, you were in Kosovo and Metohija only in 1998 and you do not know, or rather, do you know anything about the wearing of ribbons by the Army of Yugoslavia in 1999 or are you only testifying about 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can only testify on the basis of the events that I took part in and that fall in the period from the 15th of July, 1998, until the beginning of October 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just in relation to this photograph, I think that there is something that remained unclear, although you did try to explain. His Honour Judge Bonomy asked you about the man who was lying down and who was closest to the camera, and you -- and what is he wearing that is green and is that part of police gear or police equipment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In this photograph I see two members of the police who are lying on the ground. One of them is lying directly on the pavement and the other one is reclining on him. Only this member of the police who is lying directly on the pavement has a combat vest of a member of the police that is used with another type of uniform. And in this case I assume that he was wearing it because such combat vests were not made in camouflage blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Otherwise they do constitute part of the gear worn by the members thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the personal appearance of policemen, was that something that attention was paid to in the period of 1998 when you were in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout the implementation of tasks, starting from the officers from the secretariats of the Ministry of the Interior who sent us out on our assignments, and then there were soldiers -- there were officers of the Ministry of the Interior and our command of the detachment, they all gave us compulsory instructions confirming our obligation to wear uniforms and the rest of our gear in accordance with the documents regulating that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please call up in e-court Exhibit 6D768.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose document is this, sir, Mr. Paunovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need the bottom of the document, actually, in order to be able to discuss this, we need to see number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose document is this and what's the date?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: It's a document of the Ministry of the Interior, or rather, the staff of the Ministry of the Interior dated the 7th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 1 what is stated that people should take care of in terms of their conduct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is the clear instruction stated in that paragraph, that it is indispensable to ensure full control over the members of the ministry every day, demanding that they carry out their tasks professionally and responsibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Which was an obligation that we conveyed to our subordinate officers, or rather, this is an obligation of which every member of the Ministry of the Interior was made aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 6D989 is the document that I'd like to have called up in e-court now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since you have the document in front of you we can start and you can tell us about this. What kind of a document is this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Here we see a document which is called: "Rules on the armament of authorised officials and employees with specific duties," adopted by the minister of the interior on behalf of the Ministry of the Interior regulating arms of the members of the Ministry of the Interior, the type, nature, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In practice, did people comply with these rules?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In practice there was strict compliance and members of the police could not have any other weapons or equipment except for what was envisaged in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the police units, Mr. Paunovic, did you have vehicles that you got from the army; and if so, where and when did you get them, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I think that the provisions of a certain agreement, the Vienna Agreement, if I may say, the armies of the republics of the former FRY --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Vienna or Dayton Agreement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, thank you, it's based on --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I assume that the Vienna Agreement is based on Dayton Agreement. So members of the armies of the former republics of the SFRY were allowed to hand over part of their equipment to the police units, which is what these units actually did. As far as I know from that time, there was a control body also consisting of representatives of the armed forces of all the republics of the former SFRY that verified the implementation of this decision on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That answer doesn't really make any sense, with respect. What do you mean by the armies of the former republics of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. All the former republics of the SFRY, the newly established states then, had their respective armies and equipment that was used by the said armies. When the armed conflicts were over in the territory of the SFRY, I assume that it was the Dayton Agreement and the accompanying agreements that envisaged inter alia reductions in personnel levels of armed forces and the equipment used by each and every one of the armed formations of these states.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I for one do not follow this, Mr. Lukic. If you want to explain it further -- I can't believe that the weapons held by Croatia or Slovenia would have any relevance to the MUP in Serbia, but if I'm wrong about that, it would need to be spelled out clearly because I find it difficult to see which is the relevant former republic of the SFRY. Maybe it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The only connection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Maybe it's Bosnia, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The only connection is that by this agreement it was decided that some armament can be transferred from the armies to the police, so I think that's what this witness is trying to tell us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But definitely for sure that the armament of Croatia or Bosnia never ended up in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But at the stage we're talking about, Serbia is part of a federation and the federation has control of the army. So are you saying that that federation was handing over some of its weapons to the police?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm saying nothing. I can ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, no. This is what I'm not following, so it needs to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry, Mr. Paunovic. Sometimes some things that are clear to you require additional clarification for us who are outside that. So could you please explain to Their Honours what it is that we were trying to explain through this question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, if you allow me. I am sorry if I will be speaking at too great a length, but I will try to be as specific as possible. When I interpreted the provisions of the agreement, I meant the decision of principle that existed, not at any point in time did I claim - and I am strictly against that - that any equipment or weaponry from other republics landed in the hands of the members of the police of the Republic of Serbia. What I'm saying is that in accordance with the provisions of that agreement, members of the Army of Yugoslavia transferred part of their equipment to the members of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one additional question. Was the Croatian army, for instance, allowed to transfer a part of its equipment to the MUP of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I assume that that is so pursuant to the same provisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now as for these vehicles that were obtained from the Army of Yugoslavia, were they modified in any way, do you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in most of the cases we were forced to reinforce the vehicles and to put additional protection on those vehicles, in light of the fact that the structure of those vehicles as it was did not provide the adequate level of protection against the rounds and explosives used by terrorist groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And could you please tell us, how did you reinforce them, how did you do that? How did you strengthen those vehicles? Did you personally take part in any such efforts?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, since this had to do with security and safety of the police that were under my control, I did take some initiative personally and I asked the employees in a factory where I worked to weld additional steel plates on to the vehicles that we used and also special impregnated rubber that then protected us against large-calibre rounds and against mines and explosive devices that were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Anti-terrorist actions in 1998, were they carried out together with the army and why?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you move on to deal with that question, just for the sake of being completely clear about this. Included in the equipment which was transferred by the VJ to the MUP, was there weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can testify about the vehicles that I received, not about the weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, do you say you don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I know about the vehicles that I received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Paunovic, let me repeat my question. Were anti-terrorist actions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm very sorry, Mr. Lukic. There is one other matter just to be completely clear about this. You've told us about reinforcing the vehicles. Did you also change the colour of the vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that vehicles were just reinforced by using those steel plates and impregnated rubber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you did not change the colour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, in our case we did not do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What colour were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were green, for the most part they were green.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me repeat for the third time. Were the anti-terrorist actions in 1998 carried out together with the army and why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In early 1998 the terrorist groups that we targeted in our activities were very well-equipped. They had various types of equipment, and they used various types of equipment to reinforce their positions or fortify their positions, which made it impossible for the police to carry out the tasks they had been given using the equipment that they in turn had at their disposal, so that without the VJ troops and without their equipment, their hardware, we were unable to carry out the tasks that we were set. If I -- if you consider that this is relevant, I can perhaps describe the kind of equipment that we found after we carried out some anti-terrorist actions just to illustrate what we were facing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please do go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In some anti-terrorist actions, or rather, once they were over, we would find modified passenger vehicles, such as Golf cars, Wartburg cars. The parts of the vehicle behind the driver and the passenger seat were removed in order to create space where machine-guns were then mounted, large-calibre machine-guns, heavy machine-guns, and other weapons, recoilless rifles and in some cases mortars, too. Those vehicles had been modified in other ways too for use in the field. They were equipped with chains so that they could move over rough ground, off road. As for their colour, they were mostly painted camouflage green and there were also some reinforcements put in to protect additionally the -- those who drove.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me just clarify one thing for the record. It says bestrzajni recoilless rifles in the transcript. What was the term that you used?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I used the term recoilless gun or recoilless rifle, which indicates that this is a large-calibre weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did members of the KLA use mines and explosive devices?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite a few members of both the police and the army lost their lives to mines or explosive devices.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did they build fortified facilities in the territory that you passed with your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In almost all cases once the anti-terrorist actions were over, we would come across fortified facilities that were abandoned and were already derelict because we had been there, and those were fortified bunkers, connecting trenches used for the communication between those bunkers, and bunkers in villages, and there were also other ways to fortify their command posts or positions where their members were deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now let me ask you something. I don't know whether you know from your personal experience how the KLA members used the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that members of the terrorist units treated brutally both the Albanians and the police. The Albanian people were abused in the following way. Albanian civilians were used in a number of ways, and I can describe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please do go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: One, in light of the clothes worn by ethnic Albanian women, those were wide trousers and wide skirts, females were used to conceal some of the equipment and also weapons. The police personnel refrained from searching women unless female police officers were present, and in a number of cases it was -- this practice was abused and some equipment, weapons, were removed from areas in this manner. The second method that was used in fact field and that we found to be quite striking was reflected in the presence of teenagers and women accompanied by children moving through the areas where police were deployed and they were gathering information about the police in that area and relayed the information to those who had forced them to do that. There was yet another method that was quite striking. Immediately before anti-terrorist activities would begin, a certain number of women with children, with children, would suddenly leave the areas that we were supposed to enter and by their hysterical behaviour tried to confuse the police members there and to postpone the launching of the anti-terrorist actions, probably their intention was to buy some time for the terrorist groups to enable them to leave the area that was the focus of the interest of the anti-terrorist actions. I can give you other methods, but I think that this is quite enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you just this: Did you see any men carrying children in their arms?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it would happen after the end of some anti-terrorist actions that I would come across groups of civilians and one could notice the unnatural behaviour. You would see men who appeared to be of military age, fit for military service, carrying children in their arms and their mothers or other women who were present there were not carrying children.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have any personal knowledge or were you able to learn whether the children carried by these men were not actually their children?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can testify about an event in the village of Lodza near Pec where an Albanian woman approached the man who was carrying her child in his arms and took the child away because that was her child and she wouldn't allow her family to be manipulated in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it is now time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, how many women were in the PJP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In combat units of the PJP there were no women, but there were women serving in the regular police units and they were carrying out other tasks. And we would then call them in those situations when searches of female persons had to be carried out; and when it was not possible to do so, we never searched those women at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. We need to have a break at this stage, that will be for an hour. Could you please leave the courtroom with the usher, and we shall see you again at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.47 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Paunovic, may we continue?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My mistake, I started a question and then I never finished it. Were you a member of the PJP all the time or did you do some other work from 1993 when you joined until October 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I actually carried out other work all the time, regular police work in fact, at various posts. And now as for the work in the PJP, I only did that when the PJP unit got together to carry out those specific tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask you a specific question regarding some actions that you took part in, and I would now like to ask you what the preparations for an action looked like.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific. Do you mean operational preparations?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before anti-terrorist actions, who talked to whom and so on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, depending on the nature of the mission we were given, before every anti-terrorist action, we carried out the necessary preparations. The elements of those preparations are as follows. From my detachment commander we received detailed instructions about the number, type, character of the task and the axes along each of the units participating were to take, to move along, and the assessment of the forces and equipment or assets of the terrorist units that we faced. In situations where we carried out our actions together with the Army of Yugoslavia units, we received instructions from military officers, those that were issued to our superior officers in accordance with the chain of command and were in turn relayed to us. An element of the preparation for the task was familiarization with topographic maps where our positions and the axes of movement were marked and so were the other elements that maps of this nature must contain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, who made the maps that you used in the course of anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The symbols that were marked and other elements that contained those maps lead me to believe and to conclude quite conclusively that they were made by members of the VJ because we did not have the requisite capabilities or knowledge to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Once you received your task, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Once the task for my unit was defined, I further elaborated the task with the units subordinate to me and their officers in accordance with our capabilities, or rather, if it was possible with other members of the police. The motive behind it was to explain as accurately as possible the nature of the task and what was expected of each and every police officer regarding this task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What were your targets once you launched an anti-terrorist action?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: We opened fire only on those targets from which fire was opened on our units or other citizens who happened to be in that area or if they endangered them in any other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As for terrorists, did they destroy the facilities where they were before retreating? Were you able to see that for yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In most cases in the preparation stages of our anti-terrorist actions, we would encounter situations where some facilities had been booby-trapped, where mines had been laid on some roads and other devices were placed there in order to make them impassable as obstacles. And quite often on open ground the brush and the wheat would be set on fire, and that slowed down the advance of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the action at Banja, in the direction of mine, did they set fire to something else apart from the wheat-fields?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this was a peculiar action. Immediately before the action we were forced to postpone it because a large area, a large wheat-field, was set on fire, and then we came across some houses and barns that had been set on fire too. They were on the outskirts of this village, right behind this wheat-field that had been set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And how -- what did the search of the terrain look like once you pushed the terrorists back? How did the police move? What would happen?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Once we entered a certain area, either built-up area or not built-up area, the police would carry out a search operation of the terrain in order to locate the equipment, weapons, and other hardware used by terrorist groups and to ascertain that no terrorists had been left behind or that there were no civilians there who might need some assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your actions, did you use vehicles or did you walk?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: As we prepared for the action, up until the very moment when the action was launched, if security allowed that, we would use vehicles to transport the personnel up until the point where it was no longer safe to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: And then we were forced to move in accordance with the rules of tactical combat movement, in other words, on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 6D700 up on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you to look at this document from the Pristina Corps. The date is the 24th of September, 1998, if you could look at page 3 of this document. I'm interested in item 5.1, the title is: "Tasks." Are you familiar with this axis of movement and did you, in fact, participate in this action?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, since we don't have a translation of this document, I wonder if the witness could read out the relevant passage into the transcript just for the purpose of clarity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I was just informed there is no translation for this document, then I'll ask the witness to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please read this paragraph where you recognise the axis of movement.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I read. "BG 125-1, MTBR to be engaged to provide support to MUP to crush the DTS," I assume that that would mean sabotage and terrorist groups --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Forces.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, forces. Should I go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: "BG-125-1 to be engaged on the axis village of Likovac, village of Donje and Gornje Obrinje, village of Trdevac with the following task: To support the attack of the 3rd OD PJP, JSO, and a PJP company Kosovska Mitrovica, crush the sabotage and terrorist forces and take control of the following sectors: The village of Likovac, the villages of D. and G. Obrinje, and then continue or press on with the attack and in concerted action with BG-15-2 and BG-243-2 take control of the village of Trdevac, and then inflict the greatest possible losses by not allowing them to pull out from the encirclement."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you take part in this action?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Based on this paragraph, or rather, from this paragraph I know of the village of Likovac and that more or less corresponds with the date when I was there, the 24th of September, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what was the designation of your detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that would be the 3rd OD PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And, in fact, what was the designation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: It was the 35th Detachment of the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On this occasion did you encounter any civilians nearby as this action was carried out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, not in the village of Likovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did you come across any discarded weapons and equipment of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In that village we found quite a lot of weapons, weapon parts, and equipment that had been discarded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in the course of this action, did you see or hear of any massacres against civilians that were perpetrated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, but what I did notice is that when the action started six members of a company from Kosovska Mitrovica, police members, they were killed, either by mines or explosive devices or by snipers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Generally speaking, who took part in anti-terrorist actions in the fight against the KLA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Members of the police or members of the PJP and of the territorial police units from that area, both the active and the reserve force, and the Army of Yugoslavia when it did participate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see any village guards involved in these actions, local police forces, formations that were not part of the PJP or the VJ?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No. Only members of the Ministry of the Interior were there, members of the PJP, because those were the units specially trained for these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the VJ, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, needless to say the VJ too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll try to avoid asking leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting my learned friend, but there's one thing that didn't make it into the transcript. The witness said: Yes, needless to say the VJ too, when they were involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was anyone involved in the action apart from the units that were marked on the action maps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, no one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you at any time while carrying out an action notice the involvement of any paramilitary or parapolice units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have 6D692.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at page 1, item 8 of this document sir. I will read it out loud. This is a document from the Pristina Corps command dated the 7th of August, 1998, item 8 reads: "Combat group 15-3 supports the attack of the first MUP detachment in crushing the sabotage and terrorist forces along the following axis: Gorazdevac-Lodza-Rausic-Krusevac." Do you recall on or about that date, or rather, after that date you were involved in this action? Do you recognise this axis of movement that is described here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: If I look at the date of this document, if I look at the date of this document, I recognise this location called Lodza and I recognise the axis of BG 15-3 under item 8 because I certainly was in that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What we see here is the 1st MUP Detachment. At the time your own was the 37th, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The 35th. My detachment remained the 35th Detachment throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On that occasion did you see any police generals in the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Of all the situations that I faced on the ground, there was just this once in a village called Radoste or Gedza which was behind Djakovica that I noticed General Obrad Stevanovic and I never observed any other high-ranking officers in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear about anyone issuing an order to kill civilians or to wreak mass destruction against civilian property or did you perhaps yourself ever issue such an order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never issued such an order nor did I ever hear anybody else issue such an order. Quite the contrary, in fact. Throughout I was receiving orders which I always passed on to my subordinates to the effect that our role and our mission was to preserve the safety of persons, civilians, and property on the ground, be it Albanian or another ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's police officers that we are looking at, members of the PJP. Do you think they need to have a thing like this explained to them or is this something that was part of their training?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Most police members who were in my unit, the unit that I was in charge of, had completed a two- or four-year police course, police school. The principle of safe-guarding lives and property is a fundamental moral undertaking to each of those who attend it, the police schools.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember any situations where you came under fire from an area that had plenty of civilians in it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was in Lodza of all places. At one point during an anti-terrorist activity, at a certain distance we observed a rather small group of civilians and soon after realized that we were under fire from that direction. We were unable to clearly identify the source of this firing which put our lives at risk. On the other hand, we were facing a group of civilians. Therefore, we decided to take shelter behind some buildings up there that could be used for the purpose and to wait for the firing to stop before we got on with any of our activities, regardless of what else was happening on the ground. The intention behind all of this was to make sure that we in no way put at risk the lives of those civilians that we came across.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us try to sum this up. What was the goal of all the activities undertaken by the police and the VJ within the framework of their anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: As the name itself suggests, anti-terrorist activities were aimed at eliminating terrorist activities. In areas where there was no terrorist activity, there was no need for any sort of counter-terrorist activity by the VJ or, indeed, the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know whether in the summer of 1998 there were any terrorists in cities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I do know that most of their activities focused on non-built-up areas in the summer of 1998, the nearby woods or vacant areas, non-built-up areas. I'm not sure if this matters or not, but their favourite choice was blocking roads connecting towns in Kosovo and Metohija, whereby they made sure that people couldn't get on with their lives as usual in terms of travelling from one town to another. There were a number of cases in which we were forced to clear the roads connecting some of these towns.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Based on your personal experience, and you were in the area yourself, was it necessary to have anti-terrorist actions back in 1998 in order to make sure that people could get on with their lives?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Not only was this necessary. I firmly believe that this was our responsibility and not just to make sure that people could get on with their lives but also in order to safe-guard their right to life.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know exactly which specific areas members of the KLA were holding in the summer of 1992 [as interpreted] before the launch of these anti-terrorist activities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: You're asking me about 1998, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, it must be a misprint.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Based on my work on the ground and based on information I received from my superiors, or rather, my officers in the summer of 1998, most of the non-built-up areas throughout Kosovo and Metohija were entirely in the hands of these terrorist groups. As for what I myself experienced while I was in the area, the entire area behind Kosovska Mitrovica and between Kosovska Mitrovica and Pec where one finds the villages of Srbica and Rudnik and then from those villages towards such villages as Klina, which is consistent with the area that is very often colloquially described as Drenica. So all of this area was fully under the control of these terrorist groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that as these anti-terrorist actions were in progress there were any high officials of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia staying in Kosovo? Do you know if someone was perhaps spending all of their time there and do you know if perhaps there was someone else who would occasionally show up in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I told you in one of my previous answers the one high-ranking officer that I noticed at the time. As for any others, I mean high-ranking officers of the MUP or the VJ, I can only assume that they would travel to the area in order to tour their own units that had certain areas that they were responsible for.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just another question. Do you know about this incident involving a Red Cross vehicle, the International Committee of the Red Cross, during the action at Likovci, and do you know about this vehicle stumbling upon a mine?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: My officers did tell me that heavily fortified terrorist units in the area had laid mines and explosives that were meant to wreak havoc on members of the police and the VJ; as a result of this, an ICRC vehicle was damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Paunovic. For the time being these were my questions, and now you will be examined by one of my colleagues from one of the other Defence teams or perhaps cross-examined by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Paunovic. I only have a handful of questions for you. First of all, tell me what the commander of your company in the 35th Detachment was called.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of my detachment was Mr. Branko Prljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've told us that already. I was asking about the commander of your company because you said that you were deputy commander. The company was from Kraljevo, from Cacak, so yes, can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I understand what you mean, and of course I do apologise for misunderstanding your question the first time around. The commander of my company was Kresimir Krasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Maybe this is something that I missed. How many companies were there that were part of the 35th Detachment in addition to yours?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly, but I assume five or six.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'd like to ask you now a number of questions about some documents that Mr. Lukic has been showing you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have 6D692 brought up for our benefit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: You have a hard copy in front of you so my question is: When is first time you set eyes on this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I assume that I saw the document as I was being proofed for the execution of this activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that this is a preliminary order by the corps command? At the bottom of the document you have the addressees or the potential addressees. Would I be right in saying that there is not a single MUP unit on that list that was supposed to have this delivered to them and can we not see an incoming stamp of the command of the 15th Armoured Brigade, certifying that this document was actually taken delivery of at the command of the 15th Armoured Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I see on this document too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Oh, there is an interpretation of this. Am I right if I say that this preparatory order, as stated in the heading, is indeed a preparatory order and does the second paragraph say that the commanders of the units that are being issued a task through this preparatory order should come to the forward command post in order to receive this task?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot give an answer with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you to read it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Just tell me which part.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Preparatory order is the heading, not the first sentence but the second one: "On the 8th of August," et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: "On the 8th of August, 1998, at the forward command post in Djakovica all officers and commanders of the brigades are to assemble (125th and 549th mtbr) and commanders of BGs engaged in supporting MUP forces (BG-52-Radonjicka Cuka, BG-549-3, BG-125-3, and the 52nd bVP) in order to receive tasks ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any mention of any officers of any PJPs who were supposed to come and receive tasks from the command of the Pristina Corps? Am I right if I say that there is no such thing and that this is a preparatory order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this paragraph that I've read out, the only thing I can notice is what I can quote, "that are being engaged in order to support MUP forces," that is where I recognise the MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My colleague Mr. Lukic asked you something about paragraph 8 of this document, and you said that the first detachment of the MUP was your detachment, although another document it was the 3rd and in fact it was called the 35th. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My detachment was the 35th Detachment throughout in terms of the official nomenclature of the ministry, but if we look at the date and the locality of Lodza that I am aware of and I assume that this coincided with the activity that I took part in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would object, although the witness answered, but my question was whether he recognises the axis from this order, not whether his unit was marked as the 1st. He cannot know in which way military marks PJP units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, what the witness has said so far is that he assumes that this is related to something he participated in because of the reference to the locality of Lodza. Is there anything else in paragraph 8 that suggests to you that the MUP detachment referred to there is the 35th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is only the location and the date that is an association in my mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Now I would like to ask for the following document to be called up in e-court: 6D700.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, you had this in front of you and I have the same question: When did you first see this order of the command of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would object to this one also. We need first foundation whether he ever saw this one and then when he saw it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we know he's seen it, Mr. Lukic, it's already been referred to in the evidence. So there's nothing wrong with this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He confirmed only that he recognises the axis from this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, but he's seen the document, he saw it today, and if that's the first time, he can tell us that. That's all the question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Please answer. When did you first see this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say with any degree of certainty whether I first saw it then or now, but according to the elements I see now, I recognise the axis that I mentioned a few moments ago, the one in 5.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: I accept that you said this on the basis of the axis, but you see there is a major difference whether you saw something for the first time nine years ago or this week.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely, that is what I am saying now. I cannot claim with any degree of certainty that I actually did see it nine years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Am I right yet again when I say that Mr. Lukic quoted 5 and 5.1 to you, tasks, namely, that the 125th Motorised Brigade of the Army of Yugoslavia was receiving a task and it consists of the following, and you don't have to read it again. However, is this task being issued to the 125th Motorised Brigade? Is that the unit involved? 5.1.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what I see, the task is issued to the 125th Motorised Brigade that should be engaged in order to support the MUP forces to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask you something that is not related to documents. Today during your testimony you said on page 65, lines 15 and 16, in response to one of the questions put by Mr. Lukic that you received detailed from your commander of the 35th Detachment of the PJP. In relation to that I would like to ask you: How is it that you received these tasks? Was it verbally? In writing? What was the procedure involved of planning from your level to the platoons, that is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In most cases I received tasks from my detachment commander verbally, with the support of documents that he had and that could have been given to me as an officer of a lower organizational unit. These documents were excerpts from topographic maps and possibly, possibly, certain descriptive documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the same page you say, in continuation, when the units of the Army of Yugoslavia took part in some actions, officers of the VJ gave instructions to your superior officers and then they would pass that on to you. What is the source of this knowledge of yours?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In planning the action that was taking place on the outskirts of the built-up area, the town of Podujevo, facing the mountain of Bajgora, I was present myself at the command post of the officer of the Army of Yugoslavia together with my detachment commander, which is where the military officer was issuing instructions to my detachment commander and I was present and I was listening to all of that. After that my detachment commander spelled out in more specific terms the tasks that he received.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell me if you can remember who this officer of the Army of Yugoslavia was or from what brigade he came if you don't know his name and surname?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: What I can remember is that his rank was that of lieutenant-colonel, that I assume that he led an armoured mechanised unit because I noticed quite a bit of armoured mechanised equipment in the area, which is not to say that indeed he was in charge of that kind of a unit, and I think that his last name starts with a P, now was it Petkovic or something like that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now I would just like to call up yet another document, 6D667. Since you have the document before you, do you know what the source of this document was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "source," do you mean who it is that issued this document? On the basis of what I see here, I cannot see who issued this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Just one more question. And when was it that you first saw this document as it is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot assert that it's this document, but I saw similar documents in 1998 on the ground. My officers and the detachment commander showed me such documents, and on the basis of such documents I made note for myself in order to take further measures in my units.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: In relation to that, just one more question. On page 50 today, lines 10 through 20 you talked about the incident in Pec and what the reason for these ribbons and then you said the decision was made by the leadership of the PJP for such and such a reason and in accordance with the plan that was adopted. That means that the leadership of the PJP if not this one adopted similar documents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I assume that that is the case because I received instructions and documents from my own superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions of this witness, Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have a question questions as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. I am Mihajlo Bakrac, attorney-at-law, Defence counsel for General Lazarevic. A few moments ago when answering the questions of my learned friend Mr. Aleksic you spoke of a particular action when you yourself were present and you said that this had to do with the mountain of Bajgora. In order for the transcript to be clear, what year was this when this action was carried out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: When I'm talking about the action that I participated in, it was carried out in 1998, I think in the month of September, August or September 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You said that you heard an officer, commander of the Army of Yugoslavia, issuing instructions to your commander. Is that an order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: What I remember now is that the officer of the Army of Yugoslavia was speaking in an instructive fashion to my superiors. I cannot assert that it was an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you received maps for anti-terrorist actions for which you assumed on the basis of the markings on the map that they were compiled by or prepared by VJ officers. Can you explain to us on the basis of what it is that you make this assumption?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can assume that and I did assume that on the basis of the following elements: Number one, how the area surrounding a particular location was marked, and later on on the same map it's explained in a legend, where the enemy positions were marked, or rather, the positions of terrorist groups were marked in certain colours and in terms of the thickness of particular lines and so on. If necessary, I can go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Why would that be characteristic of the Army of Yugoslavia? Does MUP mark these things differently?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The MUP practically doesn't have topographic maps at all and doesn't use topographic maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say "almost does not have them," what does it mean, "almost," yes or no, do they have them? Do they not have them? Please decide on one of these possible answers.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I did not have them in the course of my own work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Excellent. You said unequivocally on page 70, line 7, that sometimes you participated in actions with the Army of Yugoslavia in actions where they took part in too. You will agree with me that on the basis of this it is unequivocal that you had actions where you participated in anti-terrorist struggle on your own, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In certain activities in certain axes, since my company was very small, I did take part in some of these actions on my own in some situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who drew your maps then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: We received sections of maps from our superior command, but it probably received it -- the full maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: From who?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: From the army I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: From the army that didn't participate, is that what you're trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: What I'm trying to say is the following: In light of the size of my unit which was part of a company, I participated in some anti-terrorist actions, lower-intensity actions, as part of a broader, more comprehensive action that involved other MUP and VJ personnel, but in my small, narrow area of action there was no need for the Army of Yugoslavia to get involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you now trying to tell us that your company never did take part in any anti-terrorist actions without the Army of Yugoslavia, although you did say something different at page 70, line 7, so you have to clarify, which is it then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will do that gladly, but please present me with clear options.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you trying to tell us that your company never participated in an anti-terrorist action without the participation and support of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No. What I said is that a part of my company --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Just a second. Please don't repeat what we've already heard. I'm asking you about your company. Are you now telling us that your company never participated in an anti-terrorist action independently without the participation of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not claiming that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Excellent. Now my question is: When your company did participate without the participation of the VJ, so the company, not your small part, who did your maps for you then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In those actions and in more complex actions where larger units participated, we received sections of maps where elements or symbols were marked; and our personnel, the MUP personnel, did not make those markings because they were not trained to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But whom did you get the sections from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: From my company commander and my company commander received it from his detachment commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I have just one question for you. How were you able to read those maps when you were unable to mark them? Is it possible for one to be able to read the map although one is unable to mark it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, well, it's quite simple to do so because we have the legend in the lower right-hand corner and it is possible to recognise the elements that are plotted on to the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Detachment commander Prljevic or your company commander Krasic, did they have military training?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, could you repeat that question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, the company commander Prljevic and, or rather, detachment commander Prljevic or company commander Krasic, were they graduates of the military academy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Based on my personal knowledge, I know that Lieutenant-Colonel Prljevic did graduate from the military academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions for this witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry to bother you with a bit of a query. Now, on page 83, in line 21, if you kindly read the question -- you can -- oh, "You said unequivocally on" -- this is what I'm reading -- "On page 70, line 7 that sometimes you participated in actions with the Army of Yugoslavia where they took part in it too. You will agree with me that on basis of this it is unequivocal that you had actions where you participated in anti-terrorist struggle on your own, right?" Answer, you gave the answer at 84, line 2: "In certain activities, in certain axes, since my company was very small, I did take part in some of these actions on my own in some situations." Now, kindly elaborate, what do you mean on your own? I mean, was it a voluntary act or -- and this was without any instructions to you from your detachment commander or your head? How could you do it on your own, because obviously you were a discipline force and I couldn't understand that. If you could very kindly help me with that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you allow me, I will explain. In all situations I participated as part of a joint, organized, and planned and prepared action in the execution of an anti-terrorist action. When certain anti-terrorist activities were carried out, given the axis that was assigned to me, that was my task, and it was a high-risk axis, my company carried out those actions in coordination with other members of other police units and army units. In other situations the task of my company or of my element of this company would be much less risky in terms of the danger that was involved than the tasks that were given to other police units, such as, for instance, securing a certain road or a route from one location to another where the anti-terrorist action had already been completed and where there was no terrorist threat. In those circumstances, it was enough to merely deploy the members of my unit. There was no need to have support from other units, be it the police or the army. And now I can give you some other situations if it's necessary or perhaps you're satisfied with the examples that I've provided, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: These situations that you've described, did they involve extract maps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, are you referring to the last situation that I described or the other situations where my unit participated without any support?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Any of them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when the task was a simple one and when it involved -- when it was a low-risk task such as securing a road, there was no need for us to have extract maps with all those elements marked on them, while in other situations when we were involved in complex security tasks but which were low intensity tasks in line with the strength of the unit under my command, we always had the extracts of those topographic maps that covered the relevant axis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Kravetz. You'll now be examined by the Prosecutor, Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Paunovic. I want to pick up from what you were just discussing now in response to questions from the Bench. You were saying, if I understood you correctly, in complex or high-risk situations you would carry out anti-terrorist actions in conjunction with other police units and VJ units. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When VJ units were involved in these actions, would their role typically involve providing fire support to your company so you would be able to carry out the tasks that were assigned to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The role of the Army of Yugoslavia was to provide fire support, that was in accordance with the rules, and they provided this fire support to eliminate certain fortified positions, such as the bunkers and other fortified facilities, because we didn't have the weapons that were needed to destroy such facilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So when you're speaking of fire support, what you mean is that it would be support that would require the use of tanks and artillery by the VJ unit, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say anything about the artillery because I did not see any artillery, but I did see armour of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, you spoke a little bit earlier about conducting search operations, searching of the terrain. When these tasks -- when you had to carry out these tasks in built-up areas, would the role of the VJ then would be to provide the fire support prior to your company entering the built-up area. Is that how it operated in practice?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No. The task was set up as follows. The police personnel within the framework of their establishment unit, in compliance with the rules of tactical combat movement, would approach built-up areas and they would encounter one of the two situations. The first situation was when we encountered no resistance from the location we were heading to, and we could simply pass through the streets of that town or village or to carry out searches of certain areas or houses in accordance with the law. So that was the first situation, when there was no resistance. The second situation was when we did encounter resistance, and if the resistance took the form of small-calibre fire we tried to locate the sources from which this threat was coming and to eliminate it by deploying our own weapons, but the weapons were always of the same power. To illustrate this, we would use the same calibre weapon to eliminate the threat. If somebody fired at us from rifles, we would fire at them from our own rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. And if I understood you correctly, these searches in built-up areas including house-to-house search operations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PAUNOVIC
